Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I confirmed on the account side that the refuel was applied successfully (2 GB added, $4.00 charge), and your line is Active with no suspension and no overdue bills blocking service. So let's move to device-level troubleshooting. I don't have direct access to your phone's diagnostics, so I'll need your help checking a few things.

Please go through these in order and tell me what you see:

**1. Check your status bar / signal**
- Do you see any signal bars (📶) or does it say "No Signal" (📵)?
- Do you see a network type like 5G, LTE, or 4G next to the bars?
- Do you see an airplane icon (✈️)?

**2. Confirm Airplane Mode is OFF**
If it's on, turn it off.

**3. Confirm Mobile Data is ON**
In your phone's settings, check that the mobile data / cellular data switch is enabled.

**4. Turn Data Saver OFF**
If Data Saver (🔽) is on, it restricts background data and can throttle speeds — turn it off.

**5. Check your network mode preference**
If your phone is set to prefer 2G or 3G, that will make data unusable and too slow for picture messaging. Set it to prefer 4G/5G.

**6. Check APN settings**
If your APN shows as incorrect or blank, reset the APN settings to default — then **reboot your phone**, since the change won't take effect until you do.

**7. Check your VPN**
If a VPN is connected and performing poorly, disconnect it and re-test.

Since your line was over its limit, the simplest first step is just to **reboot your device** — that refreshes the connection to the network and is usually needed after a data limit cutoff or a top-up.

Try the reboot first, then re-run the speed test. Let me know the result, and also tell me what you see for items 1–5, and we'll narrow it down from there.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps! Let me take them one at a time so I don't mess anything up. I'll start with the reboot, since you said that's the simplest first step.

turns.thought:
Yes — absolutely. **Airplane Mode is the root cause of the "No Connection."** It disables all wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), which is why you have no signal bars, no network type, and no data. Your refueled data is on the account and ready — it just can't reach your phone while Airplane Mode is ON.

Please do these in order:

1. **Turn Airplane Mode OFF**
2. **Turn Mobile Data ON** — your network status also shows "Mobile Data Enabled: No," so data will still not work even after airplane mode is off
3. **Wait a few seconds** for the phone to reconnect and re-register on the network, then check that signal bars and a network type (5G/LTE/4G) appear

A few notes on the rest of what you reported:
- **SIM status is Active** — good, no SIM issue.
- **VPN is connected** 🔒 — leave it for now, but once data is back on, if speeds are still slow, disconnect the VPN and re-test. A misconfigured or underperforming VPN is a common cause of slow data.
- **Wi-Fi radio is OFF** — that matches what you told me about not having Wi-Fi, so mobile data is the right path.
- **Data Roaming shows Off, but your line is roaming-enabled** on our side — you're within your home network, so roaming isn't needed here.

Go ahead and toggle Airplane Mode OFF and Mobile Data ON, then run the speed test again and tell me what you get. If there's still no connection after that, we'll move on to checking Data Saver, network mode preference, and APN settings.
turns.execution_output: User: Got it. Let me turn airplane mode off first.

turns.thought:
Good progress — you have signal back (📶¹ Poor, 2G), so Airplane Mode and Mobile Data are now working. That 2G reading is important: 2G is far too slow for modern data use, and it's likely why things still feel unusable. Let's fix the remaining three items.

Please do these in order:

**1. Turn Data Saver OFF** 🔽
Data Saver restricts background data and throttles throughput. Turn it off now.

**2. Change your network mode preference to 4G/5G**
Your phone is currently on 2G, which can't deliver usable speeds. Go to your cellular/network settings and set the preferred network mode to **4G/5G preferred** (sometimes labeled "5G Auto" or "LTE/5G"). Avoid 2G or 3G-only options.

**3. Reboot your device**
A restart is needed for the network mode change to take full effect and to re-register on the faster network. This also refreshes the connection after the data refuel.

**4. Re-run the speed test**

After the reboot you should see a stronger signal with a network type of 4G, LTE, or 5G. If the test then comes back **Poor or Fair** rather than Good/Excellent, that's when to address the last item:

**5. Disconnect the VPN** 🔒
Your VPN is still connected. A slow or misconfigured VPN is a common cause of poor speeds. Disconnect it and re-run the speed test — if the speed jumps, you've found the culprit.

To recap what we've ruled out: your SIM is Active, your line is Active on our side with no suspension or overdue bill, the 2 GB refuel is applied, and roaming is already enabled on your line. The remaining factors are all on the device side, and the 2G lock plus Data Saver are the two biggest ones.

Try those steps and let me know what the speed test and network type show afterward.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn Data Saver off first.

turns.thought:
Yes — the VPN is now the prime suspect, and the fact that you have an Excellent 5G signal makes it even more likely. Strong 5G signal plus "No Connection" is a classic sign of a misconfigured or stalled VPN tunnel routing your traffic nowhere.

**Please disconnect the VPN** 🔒 and then re-run the speed test right away.

Everything else we can control is now in a good state:
- Airplane Mode: OFF
- Signal: 📶⁴ Excellent, 5G
- Mobile Data: Enabled
- Data Saver: OFF
- SIM: Active
- Line: Active on our side, no suspension, no overdue bill

If the speed test comes back with a working connection after disconnecting the VPN, then we're done — and the recommendation is to leave the VPN off while you need reliable data, or switch to a different VPN server.

If it's **still** "No Connection" after disconnecting the VPN, don't worry — we have two more things to try, and I'll walk you through them:
1. **Reset your APN settings** to default, followed by a **reboot** (required for the change to apply)
2. Re-check that data is actually flowing

Let me know the result and we'll go from there. I know this has taken a while, but you've made real progress — we went from no signal at all to excellent 5G, so we've eliminated the big blockers.

Try the APN reset and reboot, and let me know what happens.

turns.thought:
Before I transfer you — you just gave me a crucial piece of new information, and I think I may have found it. **You're in France, which means you're roaming.**

Earlier, your network status showed **"Data Roaming: OFF"** on your device. When you're outside your home network, your phone will refuse to use mobile data unless Data Roaming is switched ON — even with an excellent 5G signal. That would produce exactly the symptom you're seeing: full signal bars, data enabled, but "No Connection."

This is the one thing we hadn't tried, because I didn't know you were abroad until just now.

**Please turn Data Roaming ON** on your device, then re-run the speed test.

The good news on my side: I've confirmed your line **555-123-2002 is already roaming-enabled** on our account, so nothing needs to be changed on our end and there's no charge to enable it. Once you flip that switch on your phone, data should start flowing.

I know this has been a long process, and I'm sorry it's taken this many steps — but this very plausibly is the missing piece. Try that first, and if it works, you'll have your 2 GB of refueled data available for the rest of the trip (through the end of this cycle on 2025-02-28).

Let me know the result, and if it's still not connecting, I'll transfer you to technical support right away as promised.
